title: Adaptive runtime receive-credit shadow foundation work item
summary: Add the bounded connection-local observation, internal forced-policy, provenance, and shadow-only receive-credit foundation while legacy_current remains authoritative.
planned_changes:
- Introduce the smallest internal receive-credit policy seam with legacy_current as the unchanged default and with internal/test-only immediate and frozen read_dominant_batch forced values.
- Preserve every existing correctness, progress, low-headroom, saturation, terminal-read, FIN, reset, cancellation, disposal, shutdown, recovery, and completed-stream guard regardless of forced or shadow selection.
- Add a compact versioned connection-local observation and immutable policy snapshot evaluated only at actor-safe boundaries, with bounded reason codes, deterministic fallback, monotonic hasIssuedApplicationData state, and no advisor dependency.
- Add observe_only and shadow plumbing with no runtime behavior consumer; shadow records the frozen legacy selector recommendation while legacy_current remains applied.
- Keep disabled observation behavior-neutral and keep steady-state observation free from per-observation allocation, global locking, per-packet evaluation, and unbounded stream enumeration.
- Add schema-backed local-result and epoch-row serialization or validation plumbing with repository, binary, workload, policy, artifact, and transformation provenance.
- Add focused requirement-home, state/replay, correctness-guard, schema, and cost coverage before running matched local forced-policy campaigns.
- Land the seam, observation, shadow, and local-evidence portions as separate interruption-safe commits when each portion passes its own verification gate.
verification_plan: Validate the touched SpecTrace artifacts individually and verify their direct links; prove the unset seam is equivalent to legacy_current; prove internal forced values cannot bypass correctness guards; prove deterministic replay and exact in-domain legacy selector agreement in shadow mode; prove sticky application-write fallback, actor-safe latching, bounded reasons, conservative recommendations for missing/stale/contradictory/out-of-domain observations, disabled-path neutrality, and steady-state allocation/lock bounds; validate representative local-result and epoch-row documents against their schemas; preserve retained negative evidence; run focused and property/fuzz tests, the receive-credit cost benchmark, matched local-only forced-policy campaigns, and the complete Release suite before marking the item complete. ProtocolLab is a later eligibility gate and is not required to complete the behavior-neutral shadow foundation.
out_of_scope: Applying active_internal controller output to production runtime behavior
Widening receive-credit batching beyond the frozen sticky read-dominant selector
Changing oversized-write admission, send planning, datagram batching, actor quantum, packet cadence, congestion control, recovery, or other policy axes
Adding a runtime-advisor dependency or a global per-connection policy manager
Using benchmark labels, payload constants, scenario identifiers, caller-visible concurrency, online learning, or live exploration as runtime inputs
Adding public API or a support promise for forced or shadow modes
Publishing performance claims or submitting ProtocolLab jobs before the local shadow and counterfactual gates pass
